## Problem 1

In ridge and LASSO regression, we would like to minimize

$$
\mbox{RSS} + \lambda \sum_{j=1}^p \beta_j^2 \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad \mbox{RSS} + \lambda \sum_{j=1}^p \vert \beta_j \vert,
$$
respectively, in order to estimate our regression coefficients. Recall that $\mbox{RSS} =\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat y_i - y_i)^2$. 


a.  How do the estimated coeffients from ridge and LASSO compare to the estimated coeffients from least squares when $\lambda = 0$?


\vspace{7em}


b.  What value will the ridge and LASSO regression coefficients approach as $\lambda \to \infty$?



c.  Let $\boldsymbol{\hat\beta} = (\hat\beta_1 = 1.5,~ \hat\beta_2 = 2.5)$ be the vector of estimated least squares regression coefficients. This vector is displayed on the plot below. Draw an arrow, starting from $\boldsymbol{\hat\beta}$ in the direction that ridge or LASSO regression would penalize these coefficients, assuming that $\lambda$ is positive.

## Problem 3

Both ridge and LASSO aim to reduce test MSE compared to least squares regression. Clearly explain, in terms of bias and variance, how these techniques achieve this reduction in test MSE. 

\newpage

## Problem 4

Ridge and LASSO are both *shrinkage* techniques, but one of them is also a *model selection* technique. State which of these techniques is a model selection technique, and make an argument (this may be geometric or algebraic) regarding how this technique performs model selection.
